title: MLB calibration is improving month over month -- but still trails the market
headline_insight: The MLB model's calibration error fell from 0.1265 in June to 0.075 in July, yet the market stayed sharper in both months (0.121, then 0.0439).
what_it_means: Splitting the record by calendar month checks whether the model is stable or drifting. MLB is encouraging -- the model got better-calibrated as July games came in (ECE 0.1265 to 0.075) -- but the market improved faster and kept its lead. Soccer stayed poor in both months: the model's monthly Brier was 0.3273 in June and 0.3346 in July, against a market at 0.1955 and 0.195.
how_to_read: Each cell is one sport-month; lower Brier and ECE are better, and the honest comparison is the model row against the market row within the same month.
why_it_matters: A model whose numbers hold steady across months is trustworthy; one whose numbers sit far from the market in every month (soccer) needs more data before any monthly split can be believed.
caveat: The June MLB month rests on only n=5030 rows and July soccer on n=3052 rows after segmentation, so the monthly split is thin at both ends.
